subject: dragonfly
pitch: An emperor dragonfly hovering above a pond. A long, slim abdomen in electric blue with black markings down its back, an apple-green thorax, huge wraparound turquoise eyes, and four glassy wings with a fine net of dark veins and a faint golden sheen, held flat and wide. Six thin legs are tucked under it.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact TypeScript model using realistic emperor dragonfly proportions, roughly 10-11 cm wingspan and 8 cm body length, and deciding on a hovering height above the pond surface for the model.

I'm sketching the construction approach: body segments built from spheres and cylinders for abdomen, thorax, and head, with wings as thin flat shapes using a subtle color or paint effect for veins and sheen rather than true transparency since materials are opaque. I'm also laying out coordinates with the dragonfly facing +Z, head forward and abdomen trailing back, keeping total length near 9 cm.

Now I'm defining the joint hierarchy and abdomen construction, planning a root thorax joint, a head joint positioned forward, and an abdomen built as a tapered sweep along a path with a radius function for the thin-thick-thin shape, plus stripe-based paint for the dark banding markings along its length.

For the path's parent I'll set it to the thorax joint since numeric path points aren't built inputs. I'm defining a radius function that keeps the abdomen thin near the thorax, widens slightly mid-length, and tapers again toward the tip to mimic the dragonfly's slender form, then sketching the thorax as a scaled sphere with a green color before considering stripe detailing.

Thinking about whether to add stripe paint to the thorax, I decide to skip it for simplicity and move on to the head, planning two large turquoise eye spheres positioned symmetrically and a small sphere for the head base.

For the eyes and face, I'm settling on dark coloring with eyes meeting near the top of the head, plus a small dark face patch between them.

Now I'm working out the four dragonfly wings — flat, wide, and horizontal, extruded from a 2D outline where the span runs along X and the chord along Z, keeping them thin and positioned above the thorax. Defining the forewing outline...

For the wing coloring, I'm designing a translucent glassy paint with a Voronoi-cell pattern to create a vein-like network across the wing surface, mixing a pale glass color with a darker vein tone based on cell edge distance, plus a subtle noise-based sheen.

Now I'm working out the hindwing outline shapes and figuring out how to mirror the wing geometry for the opposite side using cross-product math to properly flip the surface normal while keeping the extrude orientation consistent. I'm also setting up a joint hierarchy so the wings attach correctly to the thorax at a defined position and direction.

For the legs, I'm planning to use chain geometry with hip-knee-foot points, tucking them under the body, and sweeping thin capsule shapes with a dark color along each leg segment.

Setting leg chains with thorax parentage and thin sweeps for each segment, then building the abdomen as a tapering chain with dorsal stripe sectors in black and electric blue, considering segment ring markings along its length.

Moving to the head now, adding a small dark head sphere with teal eye spheres positioned near the joint, then detailing the thorax body with pale green coloring, flattening scale, and black side stripe boxes.

Now I'm placing the wing root joints on the thorax, setting fore and hind wing attachment points on opposite sides along the z-axis so their outlines extend outward with slight thickness, then checking that the wing positions don't awkwardly overlap the eyes near the head.

For the wing surfaces, I'm building a Voronoi-cell-based paint function that creates a glassy base tinted with gold sheen, overlaid with dark vein lines traced along cell boundaries using the distance difference between nearest cells to form thin crack-like patterns.

I considered adding a pterostigma dark patch near the wingtip for extra realism but decided the coordinate math was too fiddly to bother with, so I'll skip it. Now I'm sorting out imports — pulling in THREE's geometry classes and confirming that `mix` resolves to the paint blending function despite a naming overlap with the context module — before starting to define the final export metadata for the model.

Setting up builder config...

Still defining wing geometry and the chain structure for the abdomen...

Still adding joints and body parts...

Building the leg chains and sweep geometry for each leg, mirroring hip-knee-foot points by side and making sure chain names stay unique like "legFL1/legFL2".

Setting forewing and hindwing root positions and mirroring them for the right side, checking wingspan comes out to roughly 0.12 total, then verifying naming doesn't clash before finalizing the module structure.
